subject.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent

question: Must recognized subagents explicitly inherit the requester’s resolved sender-policy ceiling, or is skipping sender-policy resolution safe because another audited spawn boundary already clamps the child’s complete tool inventory?
rationale: The intended behavior is clear, but accepting an authorization exemption requires owner confirmation or source-and-runtime proof that every spawn and fallback caller preserves the requester’s restrictions.

options.title: Carry the resolved ceiling
options.body: Represent the requester’s effective sender policy in trusted subagent metadata and intersect it with the child’s normal profile and subagent restrictions.

options.title: Prove the existing clamp
options.body: Keep the exemption only after identifying the existing inherited tool clamp and adding inverse restriction tests plus real parent/child inventory proof for all relevant callers.

recommendation.title: Carry the resolved ceiling
recommendation.body: Represent the requester’s effective sender policy in trusted subagent metadata and intersect it with the child’s normal profile and subagent restrictions.

likelyOwner.reason: JerranC introduced the per-sender policy behavior whose inheritance semantics need confirmation.
